corrections.text: The article states that "Reported friction centres on two of the four" (Node.js and ASP.NET Core 2.3). The cited CPython sources also report disagreement: in the Steering Council thread, Peter Bierma wrote "I think it's very unlikely that this deadline is met" and Mark Shannon wrote that stopping development until a PEP is accepted "puts us in an awkward position", and LWN says PEP 836 "generated quite a bit of discussion, some favorable and some critical". Reported friction appears in three of the four cases; only the Kubernetes sources reviewed report none.

The article says the Kubernetes 1.37 post states that no new kube-dns packages "will be built" after v1.40. The post's wording is "It is expected that no new packages will be built for kube-dns after v1.40." The word "expected" qualifies the date, as it does for the IPVS default-off target.
